emma_support: Customer (internal repro from acme-app) reports intermittent 429s + 502s during a rollout; started after switching to rwd-large-32k for extended context. They see spikes when prefetching 40–60KB docs.
kevin_oncall: Any error payload from the API? usually shows "rate_limit" or "quota_exceeded" in body.
emma_support: Customer pasted headers and snippet — main thing: 429 responses with Retry-After sometimes present, sometimes not. Example headers:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-ID: rwd-req-87a3
Retry-After: 3
X-Model: rwd-large-32k-v1
```

Also saw: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` after a bunch of 429s.
morgan_infra: 502s can be cascade from request queue overflow. rwd-large-32k has lower concurrency windows because KV cache memory per-request is high.
emma_support: Customer says they were batching 8 requests in parallel and each request had a ~50k context (including embeddings prefetch). They rotated API keys during repro and saw auth failures 401 mixed in.
kevin_oncall: Important to separate three failure classes: auth (401), quota (429/rate_limit), and gateway (502). For quota: our per-model soft limits for rwd-large-32k are roughly 480 RPM and 36k TPM; max concurrency per-pool is 18. Extended-context variants degrade concurrency by ~2x compared to base model.
emma_support: Sent customer a suggested repro: reduce concurrent inflight to 6, drop context to 16k, and retry with exponential backoff (initial 500ms, factor 2, max 8s). Also asked them to attach full request id traces.
kevin_oncall: For immediate mitigation advise: 1) honor Retry-After header 2) implement jittered exponential backoff 3) switch to a smaller model (rwd-large-8k) for prefetching 4) enable prefix caching where possible 5) if sustained throughput required, consider Redwood Dedicated or request quota increase via account team.
morgan_infra: I'll check traces for those X-Request-ID values — if we see queue drops we can confirm fanout throttling. Also verify token bucket refill rates for their account (billing spikes can temporarily clamp tokens).
emma_support: Customer reported billing change the same day (invoicing reset) — could be transient quota rebuild. I asked them to confirm no org-wide rate limits were recently applied by their admin.
emma_support: Pasted repro steps for customer to run locally:

```
# simple repro loop (curl)
for i in {1..8}; do
  curl -s -D - \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-large-32k-v1","input":"<~50KB doc>","max_tokens":32}' \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.2
done
wait
```

Then run again with concurrency 2 and lower context to compare.
kevin_oncall: If customer can share a small blocked trace, we can correlate with per-model queue metrics and check whether fallback to a compatible variant happened (we automatically try rwd-large-16k if the 32k pool is saturated and policy allows).
emma_support: Customer replied they can repro reliably with the curl script; will run with concurrency 2 and report back. They asked what exact headers indicate a per-model throttle vs org quota.
morgan_infra: Per-model throttle usually includes `X-Model` and `X-Rate-Limit-Model` headers, and body `{"error":"rate_limit","detail":"per_model_capacity"}`. Org-level quota uses `X-Org-Rate-Limit` and `quota_exceeded` in body. If Retry-After missing, it is usually a hard drop (burst window exceeded) — we should give them clearer guidance to catch those and backoff immediately.
rate-limiter-bot: Note: automatic mitigation rule applied to this org earlier today: `burst_backoff`=enabled, `max_burst`=120 requests in 60s. Current token refill 480 RPM.
emma_support: Thanks — I'll close the loop once they test reduced concurrency. If they still see mixed 401s, we'll verify token rotation and have them test with a long-lived key. If 502s persist after throttling, escalate to infra with trace ids.
kevin_oncall: I'll open an infra ticket if you paste the trace IDs here. Also recommend we add a short KB snippet about extended-context models having lower concurrency and quoting example numbers to reduce repeated tickets.
emma_support: Agree, will draft KB and post to #docs-devex. :thumbsup:
